Command hallucinations are auditory hallucinations where a person hears a voice that tells them what to do. These can range from simple commands like "Stand up" or "Shut the door" to more threatening ones. Command hallucinations are often associated with schizophrenia, and compliance with the commands can vary.

Some questions that can help determine if someone may be experiencing command hallucinations include: "What are the voices telling you to do?", "When did your voices first start telling you to do things?", "Do you recognize the person who is telling you to harm yourself (or others)?", "Do you think you can resist doing what the voices are telling you to do?"

Olfactory Phantosmia (olfactory hallucinations) and parosmia (olfactory illusions) are distortions to the sense of smell. Olfactory Phantosmia is smelling an odor that is not actually there, while parosmia is inhaling a real odor but perceiving it as a different scent than remembered. These conditions can be caused by a range of conditions such as nasal infections, nasal polyps, dental problems, migraines, head injuries, seizures, strokes, or brain tumors. Environmental exposures can also cause it, such as smoking or certain chemicals. In most cases, these conditions will go away on their own in time.
